To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have purified and crystallized the Caf1M-C1 pre-assembly complex, and that we have obtained the first experimental electron-density map of the Caf1M subunit of the Caf1A-Caf1M complex.

we have determined the crystal structure of a Caf1M-C1 complex to 1.8-A resolution, and that the structure shows that Caf1M binds to Caf1 in a manner that is different to that observed for the Caf1M-C2 chaperone-subunits complex.
the Caf1M-C1 complex is a dimer and that the Caf1 subunit has a novel fold, with a long helix that is inserted into the Caf1M dimer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the Caf1M-Ca1 pre-assembly complex.
the structure of a Y. pestis chaperone-Caf1 subunit complex.
the structure of the Caf1M-C1F chaperone-subunits complex and the structure of the chaperone-subunil pre-assembly intermediate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a very good example of a successful structure determination project.

this study represents a successful attempt at the crystallization and preliminary structure determination of the F1 chaperone-Caf1 complex, which is the first step towards understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in the assembly of the F1 capsule.
a complete and accurate description of the structure of the Caf1M-C1 subunit complex is not available at this time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained crystals of the Caf1M-C1 chaperone/substrate complex from Y. pestis and have determined its heavy-atom derivative phases to 1.7 A resolution.
we have solved the structure of the Caf1M-CaF1 complex by MAD and MIR phasing.
we have solved the structure of the Caf1M-C1 complex to 2.5 A, using the MAD and MIR data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Caf1M-C1 chaperone complex has a very high affinity for Caf1, and the Caf1M chaperone can bind two Caf1 molecules at the same time.
the SeMet-labelled CafM-Caf1 complex is a good model for structure determination.
the F1 antigen of Y. pestis is assembled in a chaperone-substrate complex, which is a new mechanism of subunit assembly.
